	<item>
		<title>An Interactive Archive Celebrates the Wide Ranging Projects Inviting &#8216;Unruly Play&#8217;</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/unruly-play-digital-archive/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Fri, 24 Apr 2026 16:50:14 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/unruly.jpg" alt="An Interactive Archive Celebrates the Wide Ranging Projects Inviting &#8216;Unruly Play&#8217;" />"Play is how we give permission." —Vitor Freire</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/unruly-play-digital-archive/">An Interactive Archive Celebrates the Wide Ranging Projects Inviting &#8216;Unruly Play&#8217;</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/unruly.jpg" alt="An Interactive Archive Celebrates the Wide Ranging Projects Inviting &#8216;Unruly Play&#8217;" />


<p>&#8220;Play is how we give permission,&#8221; says Vitor Freire, co-founder of the Amsterdam-based studio <a href="https://www.imagination.ooo/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Imagination of Things</a>. &#8220;Permission to challenge what&#8217;s fixed, rehearse what doesn&#8217;t exist yet, and close the distance between people who wouldn&#8217;t otherwise meet.&#8221;</p>



<p>Freire and co-founder Monique Grimord take play seriously and, in a new project, their studio created a vast repository of 169 artworks, designs, games, and more that have offered an unexpected encounter with imagination and joy. From Rael San Fratello&#8217;s award-winning &#8220;<a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2021/01/us-mexico-teeter-totter-design-award/">Teeter-Totter Wall</a>&#8221; to the healing <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2024/10/wind-phones/">Wind Phone</a> project to <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2020/10/little-amal/">a 12-foot puppet</a> walking the world, <a href="https://www.unrulyplay.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Unruly Play</a> is a multi-decade archive of participatory projects, public spaces, and digital creations that invite surprise and camaraderie.</p>



<p>&#8220;Our collaborators have always asked us where our ideas come from,&#8221; Gimrod says, &#8220;and the truth is that they come from references that rarely talk to each other—it can be a seesaw through a border wall or a phone booth connected to the dead&#8230; We wanted to create unusual dialogues and support new creative practices, and Unruly Play was our answer for that.&#8221;</p>



<p>Fully interactive, <a href="https://www.unrulyplay.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">the project</a> is searchable by theme or browsable through a shuffle feature. To dive deeper into the power of play, check out <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2024/11/the-art-of-play/">this compendium</a> of artist-designed spaces.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? 		<item>
		<title>Navid Baraty&#8217;s Atmospheric Photos Explore Contrasting Scales of Time</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/navid-baraty-the-time-between-double-exposure-digital-photography/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Fri, 24 Apr 2026 12:33:01 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[cities]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Navid Baraty]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[time]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473328</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-2.jpg" alt="Navid Baraty&#8217;s Atmospheric Photos Explore Contrasting Scales of Time" />The contrasts and tensions of contemporary urban life and timeless landscapes merge in otherworldly images.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/navid-baraty-the-time-between-double-exposure-digital-photography/">Navid Baraty&#8217;s Atmospheric Photos Explore Contrasting Scales of Time</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-2.jpg" alt="Navid Baraty&#8217;s Atmospheric Photos Explore Contrasting Scales of Time" />


<p>When we consider that enormous metropolises like New York City and Chicago have only come into being within the past few hundred years, it&#8217;s impossible not to stand in awe of ancient cultural sites that have existed for millennia or geological features that expose millions—even billions—of years of the planet&#8217;s natural history. For <a href="https://www.navidbaraty.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Navid Baraty</a>, the contrasts and tensions of contemporary urban life and timeless landscapes merge in <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/navid-baraty/">otherworldly photographs</a>.</p>



<p>Baraty&#8217;s series <em>The Time Between</em> juxtaposes cityscapes with dramatic terrain, from desert dunes to snow-capped mountains. The project revolves around images in which two distinct digital photographs converge in a composite, drawing on the film technique of double exposure and exploring ideas of permanence, presence, and the &#8220;space between different scales of time,&#8221; the artist says.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1334" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-5.jpg" alt="two photographs digitally superimposed, like a double-exposure, depicting a desert lake and a cityscape" class="wp-image-473333" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-5-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-5-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-5-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-5-1536x1025.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p><em>The Time Between </em>highlights iconic skylines like Manhattan and Chicago, pairing the outlines of skyscrapers and city lights with dramatic rock formations and atmospheric effects. &#8220;The process is intentional but restrained, combining the two frames through careful blending rather than constructing or artificially generating new elements,&#8221; Baraty tells Colossal. &#8220;I&#8217;m interested in combinations that feel impossible at first, yet strangely convincing once they come together.&#8221;</p>



<p>See more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/navidbaraty/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="1330" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-6.jpg" alt="two photographs digitally superimposed, like a double-exposure, depicting mountains and a cityscape" class="wp-image-473334" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-6-640x426.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-6-960x638.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-6-768x511.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-6-1536x1021.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="2000" height="1338" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-3.jpg" alt="two photographs digitally superimposed, like a double-exposure, depicting the Golden Gate Bridge and hazy mountains" class="wp-image-473331" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-3-640x428.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-3-960x642.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-3-768x514.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-3-1536x1028.jpg 1536w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1334" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-1.jpg" alt="two photographs digitally superimposed, like a double-exposure, depicting sand dunes and the Chicago skyline" class="wp-image-473329" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-1-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-1-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-1-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-1-1536x1025.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1283" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-4.jpg" alt="two photographs digitally superimposed, like a double-exposure, depicting the Statue of Liberty and an evergreen forest" class="wp-image-473332" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-4-640x411.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-4-960x616.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-4-768x493.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/baraty-4-1536x985.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Contrast Reigns in Austn Fischer&#8217;s Conspicuous Black-and-White Photos</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/austn-fischer-fashion-photography/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 23 Apr 2026 17:30:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Austn Fischer]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[black and white]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[editorial]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[fashion]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[gender]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[horses]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[identity]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[portraits]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473283</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-6.jpg" alt="Contrast Reigns in Austn Fischer&#8217;s Conspicuous Black-and-White Photos" />Austn Fischer's work harnesses an exuberant sense of play, utilizing fashion and style to explore identity.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/austn-fischer-fashion-photography/">Contrast Reigns in Austn Fischer&#8217;s Conspicuous Black-and-White Photos</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-6.jpg" alt="Contrast Reigns in Austn Fischer&#8217;s Conspicuous Black-and-White Photos" />


<p>&#8220;I started doing photography as a way to express things I don&#8217;t understand or to convey a message I&#8217;m having a hard time explaining,&#8221; <a href="https://austnfischer.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Austn Fischer</a> says. &#8220;I often work in quite a backwards way, knowing exactly what I want to arrange in front of the camera but struggling to understand the significance in my life until I am able to reflect on it after.&#8221;</p>



<p>The Wisconsin-born, London-based photographer taps into fashion as performance, considering how our garments, style, and gestures convey parts of our identities. Contrast is key in Fischer&#8217;s work, and it emerges through unusual pairings like lace ruffs atop athletic garb or an angular, black gown with a dainty, horse-shaped wire armature. Whether a portrait or a more conceptual composition, each work harnesses an exuberant sense of play and homes in on our ability to remake ourselves anew.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2998" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4.jpg" alt="a black and white photo by Austn Fischer of david byrne underneath a light with his hand raised as if giving an oath" class="wp-image-473288" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4-640x959.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4-960x1439.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4-768x1151.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4-1025x1536.jpg 1025w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-4-1366x2048.jpg 1366w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">David Byrne</figcaption></figure>



<p>&#8220;Growing up, I had a lot of questions around my sexuality and my own experience as a man. I naturally gravitated towards fashion because of the story clothing can convey in an image,&#8221; he adds. &#8220;The colours, shape, fabric, and the way clothing wraps around a model create a unique conversation around identity and the body.&#8221;</p>



<p>Fischer has collaborated with a range of <a href="https://togetherassociates.com/artist/austn-fischer/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">editorial and commercial clients</a>, shooting Ai Weiwei with a milkshake for <em>The New Statesman</em>, for example, and David Byrne seemingly under oath for <em>Crack Magazine</em>. Whether working on a personal project or a commissioned series, the photographer transforms a largely black-and-white palette that could appear harsh into scenes exuding warmth and softness. </p>



<p>Better understanding his own emotions is Fischer&#8217;s priority at the moment, following a series of painful experiences, both personal and professional, that have influenced what and how he&#8217;s creating. &#8220;Recently, I spent two weeks from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. painting a wall in a church white over and over to understand patience and reflect on myself. I&#8217;m working a lot on understanding emotion and myself through putting my body through different tasks or challenges,&#8221; he tells Colossal.</p>



<p>Explore more of Fischer&#8217;s portfolio on <a href="https://austnfischer.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">his website</a> and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/austnfischer" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2683" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7.jpg" alt="a black and white photo by Austn Fischer of a woman in a tracksuit and frilly collar" class="wp-image-473291" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7-640x859.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7-960x1288.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7-768x1030.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7-1145x1536.jpg 1145w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-7-1527x2048.jpg 1527w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5.jpg" alt="a black and white photo by Austn Fischer of ai weiwei holding a milkshake" class="wp-image-473289" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-5-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Ai Weiwei</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2801" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1.jpg" alt="a black and white photo by Austn Fischer of two people in a crude horse costume" class="wp-image-473285" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1-640x896.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1-960x1344.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1-768x1076.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1-1097x1536.jpg 1097w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-1-1462x2048.jpg 1462w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2421" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3.jpg" alt="a black and white photo by Austn Fischer of david byrne sitting on a chair beneath hanging shirts" class="wp-image-473287" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3-640x775.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3-960x1162.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3-768x930.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3-1269x1536.jpg 1269w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/fischer-3-1692x2048.jpg 1692w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">David Byrne</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Water Samples from Around the World Melt into Dima Rebus&#8217; Dreamy Paintings</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/dima-rebus-watercolor-paintings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 23 Apr 2026 14:37:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Dima Rebus]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[watercolor]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473242</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-2.jpg" alt="Water Samples from Around the World Melt into Dima Rebus&#8217; Dreamy Paintings" />The London-based artist incorporates water samples collected from strangers around the globe.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/dima-rebus-watercolor-paintings/">Water Samples from Around the World Melt into Dima Rebus&#8217; Dreamy Paintings</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-2.jpg" alt="Water Samples from Around the World Melt into Dima Rebus&#8217; Dreamy Paintings" />


<p>The act of painting is often seen as a solitary pursuit; we picture the artist alone in a studio, working through compositional puzzles and experimenting with materials of their own choosing. For <a href="https://dimarebus.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Dima Rebus</a>, the process is collaborative, although she may or may not know the other participants. In her large-scale works, the London-based artist adds new meaning to &#8220;watercolor&#8221; as she incorporates water samples collected from strangers around the globe.</p>



<p>In her series <em>Floaters, </em>Rebus processes these crowdsourced units by freezing them with watercolor pigments, which she then allows to melt across the substrate, creating abstract color fields. She then adds figures and elements of landscape, often with a fluid, rippling effect evocative of light glinting off the surface of a lake, as aquatic themes emerge in the form of pools and swimmers.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2289" height="1070" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7.jpg" alt="a mixed-media watercolor painting of two swimmers in a dark body of water" class="wp-image-473250" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7.jpg 2289w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7-640x299.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7-960x449.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7-768x359.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7-1536x718.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-7-2048x957.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2289px) 100vw, 2289px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Noon Floaters&#8221; (2025), watercolor on paper, chemical solutions, rainwater, and water samples from strangers, 140 x 300 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<p>&#8220;Nearly every sample arrives with a letter, opening a dialogue shaped by place, mood, memory, and time,&#8221; Rebus says. &#8220;Over the years, I’ve built an archive of waters from rain, rivers, seas, oceans, and glaciers, each preserved as both material record and human message.&#8221;</p>



<p>Find more on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/nevantuznetubus/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2500" height="1668" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6.jpg" alt="a detail of a a mixed-media watercolor painting of a swimmer in a dark body of water" class="wp-image-473249" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6.jpg 2500w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6-960x641.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6-1536x1025.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-6-2048x1366.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2500px) 100vw, 2500px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Detail of &#8220;Noon Floaters&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2560" height="1399" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1.jpg" alt="a mixed-media watercolor painting of a garden glass house interior with huge lily pads in a pool and potted plants" class="wp-image-473244" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1.jpg 2560w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1-640x350.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1-960x525.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1-768x420.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1-1536x839.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-1-2048x1119.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2560px) 100vw, 2560px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Afterimage VII&#8221; (2025), watercolor on paper, chemical solutions, and rainwater, 110 x 200 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1938" height="2481" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8.jpg" alt="a mixed-media watercolor painting of a member of the King's Guard in a pool" class="wp-image-473243" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8.jpg 1938w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8-640x819.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8-960x1229.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8-768x983.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8-1200x1536.jpg 1200w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-8-1600x2048.jpg 1600w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1938px) 100vw, 1938px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Nothing Matters Until An Empty Sofa Says Otherwise 1&#8221; (2026), watercolor on paper, chemical solutions, rainwater, and water samples from strangers, 110 x 86 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2099" height="1111" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3.jpg" alt="a mixed-media watercolor painting of a meadow with trees in the background, centered on shimmering carousel horses" class="wp-image-473246" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3.jpg 2099w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3-640x339.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3-960x508.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3-768x407.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3-1536x813.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-3-2048x1084.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2099px) 100vw, 2099px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Intuitive Course VII&#8221; (2025), watercolor on paper, chemical solutions, rainwater, and water samples from strangers, 42 x 80 centimeters</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2297" height="1076" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5.jpg" alt="a mixed-media watercolor painting of a swimmer mostly submerged in a green body of water" class="wp-image-473248" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5.jpg 2297w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5-640x300.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5-960x450.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5-768x360.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5-1536x720.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/rebus-5-2048x959.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2297px) 100vw, 2297px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Morning Floaters&#8221; (2025), watercolor on paper, chemical solutions, rainwater, and water samples from strangers, 140 x 300 centimeters</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Thousands of Strips of Silk Undulate in Kenny Nguyen&#8217;s &#8216;Deconstructed Paintings&#8217;</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/kenny-nguyen-silk-textiles-paintings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 23 Apr 2026 12:15:05 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[fabric]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Kenny Nguyen]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[painting]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[textiles]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[weaving]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473254</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-1.jpg" alt="Thousands of Strips of Silk Undulate in Kenny Nguyen&#8217;s &#8216;Deconstructed Paintings&#8217;" />The North Carolina-based artist draws on his Vietnamese heritage and his background in fashion design.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/kenny-nguyen-silk-textiles-paintings/">Thousands of Strips of Silk Undulate in Kenny Nguyen&#8217;s &#8216;Deconstructed Paintings&#8217;</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-1.jpg" alt="Thousands of Strips of Silk Undulate in Kenny Nguyen&#8217;s &#8216;Deconstructed Paintings&#8217;" />


<p>Silk has been crafted in Vietnam for centuries, where it&#8217;s treasured as a lightweight, luxurious fabric used in traditional garments and art. For <a href="https://www.kennynguyen.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Kenny Nguyen</a>, who was born in Ben Tre Province and is currently based in Charlotte, North Carolina, the material provides the foundation for vibrant, large-scale wall works that combine elements of weaving and tapestries, garment production, painting, and sculpture.</p>



<p>Using thousands of hand-cut strips of silk, Nguyen draws on his background in fashion design, employing techniques such as pinning, weaving, sewing, and layering to create what he describes as “deconstructed paintings.” Each work is created around a kind of imaginary body, its creases and undulating forms evoking movement and versatility.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1864" height="876" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-9.jpg" alt="a large-scale silk and acrylic installation by Kenny Nguyen featuring thousands of strips of colorful fabric in an a textural, undulating, abstract composition" class="wp-image-473265" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-9.jpg 1864w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-9-640x301.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-9-960x451.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-9-768x361.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-9-1536x722.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1864px) 100vw, 1864px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Undercurrent Series No. 10&#8221; (2026), hand-cut silk fabric, acrylic paint, and canvas, mounted on wall, <br>64 x 158 x 8 inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>Even though the works appear fixed, they are actually very malleable. Every time a piece is installed, its undulations are determined by where the pins are placed, and it assumes something of a new version. This complements Nguyen&#8217;s approach to silk as a kind of &#8220;second skin,&#8221; he says, which adapts to its environment, represents memories and heritage, and serves as a metaphor for his personal identity.</p>



<p>Nguyen&#8217;s work is currently on view in <em><a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/textile-art-redefined-exhibition/">Textile Art Redefined</a> </em>at Saatchi Gallery in London and <em>Earth to Sky </em>at <a href="https://www.sundaramtagore.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Sundaram Tagore Gallery</a> in Singapore. His work will also be included in the exhibition <em>Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses</em> at the <a href="https://www.brooklynmuseum.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Brooklyn Museum</a>, which opens on May 16, and a forthcoming group exhibition at Sundaram Tagore&#8217;s London location. See more on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/kennynguyenclt" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-11.jpg" alt="a detail of a large-scale silk and acrylic installation by Kenny Nguyen featuring thousands of strips of colorful fabric in an a textural, undulating, abstract composition" class="wp-image-473262" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-11.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-11-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-11-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-11-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-11-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Detail of &#8220;Undercurrent Series No. 10&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2909" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3.jpg" alt="a large-scale silk and acrylic installation by Kenny Nguyen featuring thousands of strips of colorful fabric in an a textural, undulating, abstract composition" class="wp-image-473257" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3-640x931.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3-960x1396.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3-768x1117.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3-1056x1536.jpg 1056w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-3-1408x2048.jpg 1408w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Eruption Series No. 86&#8221; (2025), hand-cut silk fabric, acrylic paint, and canvas, mounted on wall, 69 x 53 x 8 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3009" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4.jpg" alt="a detail of a large-scale silk and acrylic installation by Kenny Nguyen featuring thousands of strips of colorful fabric in an a textural, undulating, abstract composition" class="wp-image-473258" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4-640x963.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4-960x1444.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4-768x1155.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4-1021x1536.jpg 1021w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-4-1361x2048.jpg 1361w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Detail of &#8220;Eruption Series No. 86&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1220" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-5.jpg" alt="a large-scale silk and acrylic installation by Kenny Nguyen featuring thousands of strips of colorful fabric in an a textural, undulating, abstract composition" class="wp-image-473259" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-5-640x390.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-5-960x586.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-5-768x468.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-5-1536x937.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Encounter Series No. 62&#8221; (2025), hand-cut silk fabric, acrylic paint, and canvas, mounted on wall, 62 x 115 x 4 inches</figcaption></figure>

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1916" height="1481" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-12.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-473325" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-12.jpg 1916w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-12-640x495.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-12-960x742.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-12-768x594.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-12-1536x1187.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1916px) 100vw, 1916px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Eruption Series No. 45&#8221; (2024), hand-cut silk fabric, acrylic paint, and canvas, mounted on wall, 83 x 113 inches (flat dimensions)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1371" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-7.jpg" alt="a large-scale silk and acrylic installation by Kenny Nguyen featuring thousands of strips of colorful fabric in an a textural, undulating, abstract composition" class="wp-image-473264" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-7-640x439.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-7-960x658.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-7-768x526.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/nguyen-7-1536x1053.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Undercurrent Series No. 5&#8221; (2026), hand-cut silk fabric, acrylic paint, and canvas, mounted on wall, 67 x 112 x 7 inches</figcaption></figure>

		<title>Tania Yakunova&#8217;s Expressive Figures Entwine with Plant Life in Digital and Graphite Illustrations</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/tania-yakunova-digital-graphite-illustrations/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>

				<category><![CDATA[Illustration]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[digital]]></category>

		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473204</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/tania-1.jpg" alt="Tania Yakunova&#8217;s Expressive Figures Entwine with Plant Life in Digital and Graphite Illustrations" />Grainy textures and gestural lines characterize the lush compositions of Tania Yakunova.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/tania-yakunova-digital-graphite-illustrations/">Tania Yakunova&#8217;s Expressive Figures Entwine with Plant Life in Digital and Graphite Illustrations</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/tania-1.jpg" alt="Tania Yakunova&#8217;s Expressive Figures Entwine with Plant Life in Digital and Graphite Illustrations" />


<p>Grainy textures and gestural lines characterize the <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/tania-yakunova/">lush compositions</a> of <a href="https://www.yakunova.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Tania Yakunova</a>. Collaborating with a range of commercial and editorial clients, the Kyiv-born illustrator harnesses the visual impact of bold shapes and vibrant color palettes to convey brand narratives and inexpressible feelings. Bare feet planted in dandelion-strewn grass and a greenhouse-style figure housing flowers attempting to burst from the glass cages, for example, conjure Yakunova&#8217;s homesickness, since she left her native Ukraine for London in 2023.</p>



<p>The artist&#8217;s distinct expressions translate across mediums, whether working in hand-built ceramic sculpture, painting, or digital and graphite illustration. Keep an eye out for new print releases and her latest projects on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/anni_tett" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/stevens-8.jpeg" alt="Vibrant Sea Creatures Spring to Life in Lisa Stevens&#8217; Textured Sculptures" />The Bristol-based artist's vibrant practice is inspired by underwater organisms. </p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/lisa-stevens-coral-sea-creatures-ceramic-sculptures/">Vibrant Sea Creatures Spring to Life in Lisa Stevens&#8217; Textured Sculptures</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/stevens-8.jpeg" alt="Vibrant Sea Creatures Spring to Life in Lisa Stevens&#8217; Textured Sculptures" />


<p>Spikes, fans, florets, waves, and other characteristics of marine creatures continue to shape the work of <a href="https://www.lisaseaurchin.co.uk/about" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Lisa Stevens</a>. The Bristol-based artist&#8217;s vibrant practice revolves around <a href="/tags/lisa-stevens">ceramic sculptures</a> inspired by sea urchins, coral, nudibranchs, and other underwater organisms. Each piece is unique, with numerous colorful glazes and textures, and they often take on a fantastical quality, incorporating hybrid features that conjure associations with celestial objects, anatomy, and other facets of nature.</p>



<p>Find more on Stevens&#8217; <a href="https://www.instagram.com/lisaseaurchin" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>, plus watch clay sculpting tutorials on <a href="https://www.youtube.com/@lisaseaurchin" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">YouTube</a>.</p>

		<item>
		<title>Animals Wander through Neighborhood Streets at Twilight in Nicholas Moegly&#8217;s Illustrations</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/nicholas-moegly-twilight-town-illustrations/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 22 Apr 2026 12:10:30 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Illustration]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[architecture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[deer]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[drawing]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[foxes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[houses]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nicholas Moegly]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473163</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-1.jpg" alt="Animals Wander through Neighborhood Streets at Twilight in Nicholas Moegly&#8217;s Illustrations" />Nightfall sets the scene for neighborhoods and quiet streets in which curious creatures roam.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/nicholas-moegly-twilight-town-illustrations/">Animals Wander through Neighborhood Streets at Twilight in Nicholas Moegly&#8217;s Illustrations</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-1.jpg" alt="Animals Wander through Neighborhood Streets at Twilight in Nicholas Moegly&#8217;s Illustrations" />


<p>In folklore, twilight is often interpreted as a liminal, even magical time during which spirits emerge in the transition between light and dark. It&#8217;s sometimes even seen as a period when extra caution is advised, as will-o&#8217;-the-wisps, shapeshifters, and fae may try to influence people in their path. For artist <a href="https://www.nicholasmoegly.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Nicholas Moegly</a>, nightfall sets the scene for neighborhoods and quiet streets in which curious creatures roam, and lights flicker on in houses, signaling the end of the day.</p>



<p>Many of <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/nicholas-moegly/">Moegly&#8217;s works</a> possess a dreamy realism along the lines of photographer Todd Hido&#8217;s <em><a href="http://www.toddhido.com/homes" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Houses at Night</a></em> or the illustrations of children&#8217;s book author <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Van_Allsburg" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Chris Van Allsburg</a>. There is both a timelessness and a sense that these locations could represent virtually anywhere around the U.S. Sometimes, deer and foxes meander through yards or down alleyways, glancing backward as if responding to a sound. In other compositions, lights shine from upper windows of a house or shop on a hazy street corner, although people are nowhere to be seen.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="824" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-4.jpg" alt="an illustration by Nichols Moegly of a fox wandering in a street, illuminated by a street light at dusk" class="wp-image-473167" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-4-640x264.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-4-960x396.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-4-768x316.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-4-1536x633.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;A Suspended State&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<p>Moegly is currently in the midst of the largest oil painting he&#8217;s made thus far, experimenting with the relationship between scale and realism in a way that&#8217;s challenging his artistic direction. He&#8217;s also working toward future exhibitions, transitioning from online releases to more in-person shows. See more on his <a href="https://www.instagram.com/nicholasmoegly" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1200" height="1450" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-3.jpg" alt="an illustration by Nicholas Moegly of a simple gabled house with a light on upstairs, in the evening" class="wp-image-473166" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-3.jpg 1200w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-3-640x773.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-3-960x1160.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-3-768x928.jpg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;A Summer&#8217;s End&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1700" height="899" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-2.jpg" alt="an illustration by Nichols Moegly of a deer wandering in a street, illuminated by a street light at dusk" class="wp-image-473165" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-2.jpg 1700w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-2-640x338.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-2-960x508.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-2-768x406.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-2-1536x812.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1700px) 100vw, 1700px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;A Constant Search&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1200" height="1680" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-8.jpg" alt="an illustration by Nicholas Moegly of a small town corner store with a light on upstairs, in the evening" class="wp-image-473171" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-8.jpg 1200w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-8-640x896.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-8-960x1344.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-8-768x1075.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-8-1097x1536.jpg 1097w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Whestel&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1200" height="1631" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-6.jpg" alt="an illustration by Nichols Moegly of a fox wandering near a retro gas station, illuminated by a street light at dusk" class="wp-image-473169" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-6.jpg 1200w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-6-640x870.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-6-960x1305.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-6-768x1044.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-6-1130x1536.jpg 1130w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;An Old Friend&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1200" height="1450" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-5.jpg" alt="an illustration by Nichols Moegly of deer wandering in a street, illuminated by a street light at dusk" class="wp-image-473168" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-5.jpg 1200w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-5-640x773.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-5-960x1160.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/moegly-5-768x928.jpg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1200px) 100vw, 1200px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;An Inevitable Fate&#8221;</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>How One Cooperative Champions the Quechua Weavers of Peru&#8217;s Sacred Valley</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/awamkai-peru-sacred-valley-weavers/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 21 Apr 2026 20:48:39 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Climate]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Craft]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Partner]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Awamaki]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Indigenous culture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Peru]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[weaving]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=472003</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-.jpg" alt="How One Cooperative Champions the Quechua Weavers of Peru&#8217;s Sacred Valley" />"Some people say, ‘Why do you weave?’ But they don’t understand this work."</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/awamkai-peru-sacred-valley-weavers/">How One Cooperative Champions the Quechua Weavers of Peru&#8217;s Sacred Valley</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-.jpg" alt="How One Cooperative Champions the Quechua Weavers of Peru&#8217;s Sacred Valley" />


<p>The economy of Peru&#8217;s Sacred Valley has long been entwined with the seasons. Rural communities typically grow crops and raise livestock to sustain themselves and to barter with others, a process that necessitates an attunement with nature, its cycles, and how these patterns influence self-sufficiency.</p>



<p>This is particularly true for the <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quechua_people" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Quechua communities</a>, Indigenous peoples who have long worked for subsistence rather than state currencies. In recent years, health clinics, schools, markets, and transportation requiring residents to use cash have slowly eroded this way of life. Today, many Quechua men leave their communities to work in tourism, which offers an income and the opportunity to learn Spanish. Conversely, women often remain at home to care for children and farms, making them dependent on support from their partners and family members.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-embed is-type-video is-provider-vimeo wp-block-embed-vimeo"><div class="wp-block-embed__wrapper">
<iframe loading="lazy" title="Land and Looms | Awamaki" src="https://player.vimeo.com/video/228854621?dnt=1&amp;app_id=122963" width="500" height="338" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin"></iframe>
</div></figure>



<p>In 2009, the nonprofit <a href="https://www.awamaki.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Awamaki</a> formed to aid communities around Ollantaytambo, Cusco, as they navigated this change. U.S.-based Kennedy Leavens and Miguel Galdo, of Peru,&nbsp;had worked together previously at a similar organization supporting 10 women weavers from Patacancha. When that project shuddered, the two decided to found Awamaki to maintain their support.</p>



<p>The nonprofit grew quickly, and today, it assists nine cooperatives, comprising 174 artisans and community members who work across craft and tourism. With collaboration at its core, Awamaki prides itself on sustainability and focuses on broadening its partners&#8217; access to a diverse array of markets and economic opportunities.</p>



<p>In addition to financial changes, the climate crisis is rapidly transforming the ways of the Sacred Valley, which faces disproportionate impacts as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2025/jun/22/peru-quechua-pacha-mama-andes-way-of-life-in-pictures" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">glaciers melt</a> and the water supply dwindles. &#8220;The shift towards having personal income, for our artisan partners, is not about replacing traditional livelihoods, but about widening the economic ground beneath them so they can move their families towards prosperity and build resiliency to the effects of climate change, all without leaving the community or traditional ways of life,&#8221; the nonprofit tells us. </p>



<p>Partnering with Awamaki allows cooperative members to focus on traditional spinning, dyeing, and weaving traditions, while the nonprofit offers structural support in selling their goods and coordinating tourism. Carving through the terrain north of Cusco, the Andean highlands were once home to the Incans and still hold traces of the ancient empire, like the historic city of Machu Picchu, which continues to attract around <a href="https://www.culturacusco.gob.pe/unidad-desconcentrada-del-parque-arqueologico-nacional-de-machupicchu/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">one million people</a> from around the globe each year. For many years, the organization says, visitors would arrive in villages without prior notice, and the women would halt their work to meet tourists and hopefully, sell a piece.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7.jpg" alt="a woman in traditional Peruvian clothing shows something to a man in a hoodie and jeans" class="wp-image-472013" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamkai-7-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>And of course, this way of making is demanding, as women not only weave, but also raise alpacas, shear their wool, and spin and dye the soft fibers into yarn. “Before weaving, I have to wash my hands carefully so the wool doesn’t get damaged. It requires attention and care,&#8221; Ricardina, an Awamaki member from the Cusci Qoyllur cooperative, tells us. “Sometimes I can weave more, sometimes less. It depends on time, on my children, on everything else I have to do.”</p>



<p>Today, Awamaki helps to coordinate tourism and provide compensation for visits. This includes programs like <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2025/11/murmur-ring-peru-sacred-valley-immersion/">Murmur Ring&#8217;s immersion</a>, which will bring a group of creatives to the region this June. &#8220;Our role is to create opportunities that can be compatible with cultural continuity, if that is what communities themselves want,&#8221; they say, adding:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p>For women, without personal income, everyday decisions can feel distant. Paying for school supplies, buying medicine, covering transportation costs, buying food to supplement the limited traditional crops that grow at high altitude–all of these depend on uncertain flows of money and shifting household dynamics. As climate patterns grow more erratic, with harsher frosts, longer dry spells, and thinning pasture, even the agricultural base families rely on has become less predictable, deepening that sense of financial fragility.</p>
</blockquote>



<p>This regular support has simultaneously buoyed many women to greater financial independence and helped retain their way of life. &#8220;When new artisans join a cooperative, they are typically mentored by other women in their own community. Cultural knowledge remains community-held and community-led,&#8221; the nonprofit shares.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-6.jpg" alt="two people's hands holding raw and spun wool" class="wp-image-472010" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-6-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-6-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-6-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-6-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>“In my family, we make decisions together—about how to earn and how to move forward,&#8221; Daniela, a weaver from the Puskariy Tika cooperative, says. “Through this work, we are able to keep going and improve our lives little by little.”</p>



<p>Nadia, of the Rumia cooperative, echoes this sentiment. “Being part of Awamaki changed things for us. Now we have a steady income, and that allows us to keep weaving,&#8221; she says. &#8220;In our community, it’s not always easy. Some people say, ‘Why do you weave?’ But they don’t understand this work&#8230; We also teach our children to care for the environment, to grow things, to respect the land. That’s part of our work, too.”</p>



<p>To learn more about the women and support their work, visit <a href="https://www.awamaki.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Awamaki&#8217;s website</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1.jpg" alt="a collection of yarn and natural dye materials" class="wp-image-472006" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1-640x800.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1-960x1200.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1-768x960.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1-1229x1536.jpg 1229w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/awamaki-1-1638x2048.jpg 1638w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Stained Glass Objects by Pia Hinz Reflect the Contrast Between Strength and Fragility</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/pia-hinz-stained-glass-sculptures/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Jackie Andres]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 21 Apr 2026 12:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[glass]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[light]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Pia Hinz]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[stained glass]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473023</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-2-e1776621947283.jpg" alt="Stained Glass Objects by Pia Hinz Reflect the Contrast Between Strength and Fragility" />The artist “questions our relationship to objects, their use value, and their narrative potential.”</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/pia-hinz-stained-glass-sculptures/">Stained Glass Objects by Pia Hinz Reflect the Contrast Between Strength and Fragility</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-2-e1776621947283.jpg" alt="Stained Glass Objects by Pia Hinz Reflect the Contrast Between Strength and Fragility" />


<p>Building sites and agricultural areas are typically described by the utilitarian operations that shape them—rugged, harsh, and often back-breaking. They are spaces that resist softness, built quite literally around force and tension. Artist <a href="http://piahinz.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Pia Hinz</a> flips this idea on its head as she explores the conceptual and material relationship between strength and vulnerability.</p>



<p>Living and working between Ardèche, Amsterdam, and Arles, France, Hinz has been working with <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/stained-glass/">stained glass</a> for the past three years. She focuses much of her work on objects that one might find in environments of labor, such as construction or farming. Her sculptures take on an array of recognizable forms including hammers, screws, traffic cones, tractor doors, scythes, rope, and more.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1347" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-4.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of a hammer" class="wp-image-473012" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-4-640x431.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-4-960x647.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-4-768x517.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-4-1536x1034.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;MARTEAU&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>



<p>By introducing glass, Hinz subverts the practical purpose of tools and machinery as each object emerges antithetical to its original form. &#8220;Here, fragility and invincibility intertwine,&#8221; says an exhibition statement from <a href="http://lamenuiserie2.com/en/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">La Menuiserie 2</a>, a residency the artist completed in 2024. &#8220;By replacing functional materials with fragile ones, the artist questions our relationship to objects, their use value, and their narrative potential.&#8221;</p>



<p>As light passes through the artist&#8217;s work, it spills across surrounding spaces and results in shifts of color. Pieces like &#8220;MON PRÉCIEUX&#8221; and &#8220;Néon sacré&#8221; are elegantly adorned with abstract, geometric patterns that are shaped by winding metal lines. For Hinz, working with the material is, as she describes, an &#8220;urge to retrace the relation between light and space.&#8221;</p>



<p>The artist is currently working on a permanent stained glass monument for a building in Paris. Find more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/piahinzpiahinz?utm_source=ig_web_button_share_sheet&amp;igsh=ZDNlZDc0MzIxNw==" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-13.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of screws" class="wp-image-473021" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-13.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-13-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-13-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-13-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-13-1536x1152.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;VIS&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1968" height="2438" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of a shopping cart resting on a checkered floor, with its many colors reflecting on the walls" class="wp-image-473014" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6.jpg 1968w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6-640x793.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6-960x1189.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6-768x951.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6-1240x1536.jpg 1240w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-6-1653x2048.jpg 1653w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1968px) 100vw, 1968px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">untitled (2025)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2667" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of a tractor door. its window features a green and red abstract pattern" class="wp-image-473020" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-12-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;MON PRÉCIEUX&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1490" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-1.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of chains" class="wp-image-473009" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-1-640x477.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-1-960x715.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-1-768x572.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-1-1536x1144.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;CHAINE&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1821" height="2428" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10.jpg" alt="a framed stained glass work by Pia Hinz featuring curved lines" class="wp-image-473018" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10.jpg 1821w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-10-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1821px) 100vw, 1821px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;MACHINE PICARDIE 2&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1821" height="2428" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of a scythe" class="wp-image-473016" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8.jpg 1821w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8-640x853.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8-960x1280.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8-768x1024.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8-1152x1536.jpg 1152w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-8-1536x2048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1821px) 100vw, 1821px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;PLOT&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-7.jpg" alt="a glass sculpture by Pia Hinz of a hammer" class="wp-image-473015" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-7-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-7-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-7-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/hinz-7-1536x1152.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;MARTEAU 1&#8221; (2024)</figcaption></figure>
